fully_resolved_entries.suggested_fix_before_reconciliation: Change Orders. Any change in the details of a Work Order, any schedule or exhibit thereto, or any other term of this Agreement, or the assumptions upon which the Work Order is based (including, but not limited to, changes in an agreed starting date for a Project or suspension of the Project by Sponsor) may require changes in the budget and/or timelines, and shall require a written amendment executed by duly authorized representatives of both parties (a "Change Order"). Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or course of conduct shall modify or amend this Agreement, any Work Order, or any Change Order. Both parties agree to act in good faith and promptly when considering a Change Order requested by the other party. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor's changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project's scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT

This Master Services Agreement (“Agreement”) is made between Sunesis Pharmaceuticals, Inc. which has a place of business at 341 Oyster Point Boulevard, South San Francisco, California 94080 (hereinafter “Sponsor”), and Quintiles, Inc. a North Carolina corporation having a place of business at 10245 Hickman Mills Drive, Kansas City, MO 64137 (hereinafter “Quintiles”). When signed by both parties, this Agreement will set forth the terms and conditions under which Quintiles agrees to provide certain services to Sponsor as set forth herein.

Recitals:

Sponsor is in the business of drug discovery, research and development for various pharmaceutical products. Quintiles is in the business of providing drug development and manufacturing services, clinical trial services, and other services for the pharmaceutical, medical device and biotechnology industries.

Sponsor and Quintiles desire to enter into this Agreement to provide the terms and conditions upon which Sponsor may engage Quintiles from time-to-time to provide services for individual studies or projects by executing individual Work Orders (as defined below) specifying the details of the services and the related terms and conditions.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Scope of the Agreement; Work Orders; Nature of Services; Transfer of Obligations.

Scope of Agreement. As a “master” form of contract, this Agreement allows the parties to contract for multiple projects through the issuance of multiple Work Orders (as discussed in Section 1.2 below), without having to re-negotiate the basic terms and conditions contained herein. This Agreement covers the provision of services by Quintiles and Quintiles’ corporate affiliates (see Section 16.1) and, accordingly, this Agreement represents a vehicle by which Sponsor can efficiently contract with Quintiles and its corporate affiliates for a broad range of specific services.

Work Orders. The specific details of each project under this Agreement (each “Project”) shall be separately negotiated and specified in writing on terms and in a form acceptable to the parties (each such writing, a “Work Order”). A sample Work Order is attached hereto as Exhibit A. Each Work Order will include, without limitations, the scope of work, timeline(s), and budget and payment schedule. Each Work Order shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including (when applicable) the terms and conditions set forth in the quality requirement agreement to be completed by the parties which will be made part of and attached to this Agreement (the “Quality Agreement”), in addition to the specific details set forth in the Work Order.

Integration; Precedence. Any Work Order or Change Order (as defined in Section 4.0 below) and other exhibits issued and executed pursuant to this Agreement will be made part hereof and incorporated herein by reference. To the extent any terms or provisions of a Work Order or Change Order conflict with the terms and provisions of this Agreement, the terms and provisions of this Agreement shall control, except to the extent that the applicable Work Order or Change Order expressly and specifically states an intent to supersede the Agreement on a specific matter.

Nature of Services. The services covered by this Agreement may include expert consultation, clinical trial services, statistical programming and analysis, clerical, project management, central laboratory services, preclinical services, pharmaceutical sciences services, and related data processing, data management and regulatory services, and other research and development services requested by Sponsor and agreed to by Quintiles as set forth in the relevant Work Order (collectively, the “Services”).

Transfer of Obligations. Quintiles and Sponsor, where appropriate, shall cooperate in the completion of a Transfer of Obligations Form in conjunction with the relevant Work Order. Any responsibilities not specifically transferred in the Transfer of Obligations Form shall remain the regulatory responsibility of Sponsor. The Transfer of Obligations Form will be filed with the Food and Drug Administration (“FDA”) by Sponsor where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

explanation_call.reason: As currently drafted, the clause contains no late-payment remedy — no interest, suspension right, or other consequence — leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual leverage if Sponsor delays payment beyond the thirty (30) day period, which directly threatens the cash-neutrality objective the clause purports to protect. The clause also defers all fee-calculation methodology to each Work Order without requiring that Work Orders specify the basis of calculation (fixed-fee, time-and-materials, or otherwise), creating a risk that disputed Work Order terms could leave Quintiles unable to enforce its fee entitlement. Additionally, there is no mechanism to adjust fees if the scope of Services changes, exposing Quintiles to uncompensated scope creep between Work Order amendments.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Payment of Fees and Expenses. Sponsor will pay Quintiles for fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order, which shall specify the basis of fee calculation (whether fixed-fee, time-and-materials, or otherwise). Sponsor agrees that the budget and payment schedule for each Work Order will be structured in an effort to maintain cash neutrality for Quintiles (with respect to the payment of professional fees, pass-through costs and otherwise); any change in the scope of Services shall be documented in a written amendment to the applicable Work Order with fees adjusted accordingly. Unless otherwise agreed in a particular Work Order, the following shall apply: (a) Quintiles will invoice Sponsor monthly for the fees, expenses and pass-through costs incurred in performing the Services; and, (b) Sponsor shall pay each invoice within thirty (30) days of receipt of the invoice. Any undisputed amounts not paid within such thirty (30) day period shall accrue interest at one and one-half percent (1.5%) per month, or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is less. If any portion of an invoice is disputed, then Sponsor shall pay the undisputed amounts as set forth in the preceding sentence and the parties shall use good faith efforts to reconcile the disputed amount as soon as practicable.

Let me analyze the clause text against each criterion carefully from the perspective of representing Quintiles, Inc.

The clause is about Payment of Fees and Expenses in a Master Services Agreement where Quintiles is the service provider and Sponsor is the paying party.

Let me evaluate each criterion:

**FEE-01: Are the fees stated or determinable?**
The clause says fees are "in accordance with the budget and payment schedule contained in each Work Order." This is a specific reference to where fees are set (Work Orders). This meets the criterion.

**FEE-02: How are fees calculated?**
The clause references "fees, expenses and pass-through costs in accordance with the budget and payment schedule." It doesn't explicitly state whether fees are fixed, time-based, or usage-based. 

The clause does mention the budget will maintain "cash neutrality for Quintiles," which hints at the cost basis without specifying a concrete calculation method like hourly rates or fixed fees. Since the actual basis is deferred entirely to the Work Orders rather than described here, I'm leaning toward marking this as not met.

For invoicing, the clause states Quintiles invoices monthly for fees and expenses, so timing is clear, but the calculation method isn't specified, making it only partly met. Payment is due within thirty days of invoice receipt, which is a definite answer.

On whether fees are fixed or changeable, the clause stays silent, so that's not met - and since there's no fee-change mechanism described at all, the follow-up question about whether such changes are limited doesn't really apply here.

For invoice disputes, the clause allows disputing a portion of an invoice while requiring payment of undisputed amounts, with "good faith efforts to reconcile" the disputed portion - this gives a right to dispute, a treatment for the disputed amount, and a process, though the process language is vague and timing is loose ("as soon as practicable").

Looking at the criteria more carefully, since both treatment and process are present (even if imprecise), this technically satisfies "Met" rather than "Partly met." But I should check whether the perspective matters here - FEE-07 concerns the paying party's obligations, and I want to make sure I'm applying the right lens.

For FEE-08, there's no interest, suspension, or other late payment consequence mentioned, so that's "Not met." For FEE-09, expenses are described as billed separately and invoiced monthly, but there's no approval rule or cap mentioned, which points toward "Partly met."

Suspension isn't addressed anywhere in the clause, so FEE-10 is "Not applicable." Pulling this together, my final answers are: FEE-01 Met, FEE-02 Not met, FEE-03 Partly met, FEE-04 Met, FEE-05 Not met, FEE-06 Not applicable, FEE-07 Met, FEE-08 Not met, FEE-09 Partly met, and FEE-10 Not applicable.

Each Change Order shall detail the requested changes to the applicable task, responsibility, duty, budget, timeline or other matter. The Change Order will become effective upon the execution of the Change Order by duly authorized representatives of both parties, and the parties will agree upon a reasonable period of time within which Quintiles shall implement the changes. Without limiting the foregoing, Sponsor agrees that it will not unreasonably withhold approval of a Change Order, if the proposed changes in budgets or timelines result from, among other appropriate reasons, forces outside the reasonable control of Quintiles or Sponsor's changes in the assumptions upon which the initial budget or timelines were based, including, but not limited to, the assumptions set forth in the budget or timelines. Quintiles reserves the right to postpone effecting material changes in the Project's scope until such time as the parties agree to and execute the corresponding Change Order. For any Change Order that affects the scope of the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles, Quintiles and Sponsor shall execute a corresponding amendment to the Transfer of Obligations Form. Sponsor shall file such amendment where appropriate, or as required by law or regulation.

explanation_call.reason: As currently drafted, this clause is entirely one-sided: it defines and protects only "Sponsor Confidential Information," leaving Quintiles, Inc. with no contractual protection for its own proprietary methodologies, systems, and data shared during performance of the Services. The clause also imposes no express standard of care on either party, meaning Quintiles, Inc. has no defined benchmark against which its handling obligations are measured, exposing it to open-ended liability for any disclosure. Additionally, the absence of a return or destruction obligation means Sponsor retains possession of Quintiles, Inc.'s information indefinitely after the Agreement ends, with no mechanism for Quintiles, Inc. to reclaim or secure its own confidential materials.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, each party and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to the other party. All such data and information ("Confidential Information"), written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to the receiving party and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and the sole property of the disclosing party. Each party shall protect the other party's Confidential Information using no less than the same degree of care it uses to protect its own confidential information, but in no event less than reasonable care. Upon the written request of the disclosing party, or upon expiration or termination of this Agreement, the receiving party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the disclosing party.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Confidentiality.

Sponsor Confidential Information. It is understood that during the course of this Agreement, Quintiles and its employees may be exposed to data and information that are confidential and proprietary to Sponsor. All such data and information (hereinafter “Sponsor Confidential Information”) written or verbal, tangible or intangible, made available, disclosed, or otherwise made known to Quintiles and its employees as a result of Services under this Agreement shall be considered confidential and shall be considered the sole property of Sponsor.

Quintiles Confidential Information. All information regarding Quintiles’ operations, methods, and pricing and all Quintiles’ Property (as defined in Section 6.2 below), disclosed by Quintiles to Sponsor in connection with this Agreement is proprietary, confidential information belonging to Quintiles (the “Quintiles Confidential Information”).

Confidentiality Obligations. For the purposes of Sections 5.3 and 5.4, Confidential Information shall mean both Sponsor Confidential Information and Quintiles Confidential Information. Each party hereunder agrees that Confidential Information disclosed by one party to the other shall be clearly marked ‘confidential’, or if disclosed orally, is confirmed in writing as having been disclosed as confidential or proprietary of the disclosing party within thirty (30) days after such disclosure. Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement. The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party’s obligations hereunder. Except as otherwise expressly authorized in this Agreement, each party agrees that it will not make copies or duplicates of any Confidential Information, or reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information of the other party to any third party without the prior written consent of the disclosing party. Each party agrees that it will not disclose the terms of this Agreement or any Work Order to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which shall not unreasonably be withheld. These obligations of confidentiality and nondisclosure shall remain in effect for a period often (10) years after the completion or termination of the applicable Work Order.

The foregoing obligations shall not apply to Confidential Information to the extent that it: (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than as a result of a disclosure by the receiving party; (b) becomes available to the receiving party on a non-confidential basis from a source which is not prohibited from disclosing such information; (c) was developed independently of any disclosure by the disclosing party or was known to the receiving party prior to its receipt from the disclosing party, as shown by receiving party’s contemporaneous written evidence; or, (d) is required by law or regulation to be disclosed, provided that the receiving party shall provide prompt notice of such requirement to the disclosing party to enable the disclosing party to seek a protective order or otherwise prevent or restrict such disclosure.

thinking_trace.extraction_thinking:
Let me carefully evaluate each criterion against the clause text, keeping in mind that I'm representing Quintiles, Inc.

**CON-01**: Does the clause require the receiving party to keep information confidential and limit how it is used?
- Para F7349A5F states: "The Confidential Information shall be used by the receiving party and its employees only for purposes of performing the receiving party's obligations hereunder." - This limits use.
- Also: "each party agrees that it will not... reveal, publish or otherwise disclose the Confidential Information" - non-disclosure.
- Both non-disclosure and limit on use are stated. MET.

**CON-02**: Is confidential information identified by a definite description (categories, marking or a defined test)?
- F7349A5F requires marking as "confidential" or written confirmation within 30 days for oral disclosures, but B8CBFCE3 broadens Sponsor CI to cover essentially all information made available under the agreement regardless of marking, and EC1E080F separately defines Quintiles' own confidential information. These definitions seem to conflict or layer on top of each other, so I need to reconcile how they interact.

There's a real asymmetry here from Quintiles' perspective: Sponsor CI is automatically confidential without any marking, while the combined definition in F7349A5F imposes a marking requirement. I'm leaning toward "Partly met" since the Sponsor CI definition stays open-ended, though the marking test in F7349A5F does provide some definiteness - but then I notice that clause requires information to be clearly marked "confidential," which may actually cut against treating this as fully satisfied.

For the standard of care question, I'm checking F7349A5F and DDD4C048 for any named standard like "reasonable care" or "same care as own information" - I don't find one, so that criterion isn't met. For exceptions, DDD4C048 lists four: public domain, non-restricted source, independent development or prior knowledge, and legal requirement - that's sufficient to mark this criterion as met.

For disclosure required by law, DDD4C048(d) requires the receiving party to give prompt notice so the disclosing party can seek protection - the notice standard is vague ("prompt") but the requirement itself exists, so I'll mark this met.

Now checking mutuality - both parties are nominally bound under F7349A5F, but there's an asymmetry since B8CBFCE3 makes all Sponsor information automatically confidential without marking, while Quintiles' CI is defined by specific categories and subject to a marking requirement.

For duration, F7349A5F states obligations last ten years post-completion (the "often" appears to be an OCR typo for "of ten"), so a definite term is clearly stated and met.

Moving to CON-08, I need to check whether the clause addresses returning or destroying confidential information when the agreement ends, but this doesn't appear to be addressed in the target language.

For CON-09, the need-to-know provision in F7349A5F seems to describe sharing between Quintiles and Sponsor rather than internal distribution to employees, and there's no explicit requirement that internal recipients be bound by confidentiality obligations. Since both elements - need-to-know limits and binding internal recipients - must be present and neither is clearly stated, I'll mark this as not met.

explanation_thinking_by_para.F7349A5F:
The key issue identified is that the confidentiality obligation to disclose only on a "need-to-know basis" does not require that the recipients (employees, subcontractors, etc.) be bound by confidentiality obligations. The current language limits disclosure to those who "need to know" but fails to require that those individuals are themselves bound by written confidentiality obligations comparable to those in the Agreement.

The specific evidence quote: "Quintiles and Sponsor each agree that it will only provide Confidential Information to the other party on a need-to-know basis and to the extent that Confidential Information is required for its undertaking of this Agreement."

The problem here is twofold:
First, the need-to-know restriction oddly applies only to disclosure "to the other party," when it should really govern internal disclosure to employees and subcontractors. Second, there's no requirement that anyone receiving the Confidential Information on that basis is actually bound by confidentiality obligations themselves, leaving sub-disclosure to employees and third parties unprotected.

I need a surgical fix amending the sentence about employee use of Confidential Information to require that such employees (and potentially subcontractors) are bound by confidentiality obligations at least as protective as those in the Agreement before they can receive the information.

I'm also noticing the "need-to-know" sentence itself is poorly worded—it seems to describe disclosure between the two parties rather than internal disclosure to employees/subcontractors who need to know. That sentence should be clarified to properly target internal sub-disclosure, paired with the binding confidentiality requirement.

suggestions.reason: The need-to-know restriction as currently drafted does not require that employees, agents, or subcontractors of either party who receive Confidential Information are themselves bound by written confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement. This creates a material gap for Quintiles, Inc.: Sponsor's personnel or contractors could receive Quintiles' proprietary information on a purported "need-to-know" basis with no enforceable downstream obligation to protect it, exposing Quintiles to uncontrolled dissemination of its Confidential Information without recourse against individual recipients. The companion sentence limiting use to "employees" compounds this risk by failing to impose accountability on the receiving party for any breach by those individuals. Given the ten-year confidentiality tail tied to Work Order completion, this unaddressed gap could leave Quintiles' Confidential Information unprotected throughout a substantial post-engagement period.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Ownership and Inventions; No Implied Rights.

Sponsor’s Property. Sponsor’s property shall mean any invention, trade secret or know-how related to or derived from any materials, documents, programs or information belonging to Sponsor and supplied to Quintiles pursuant to this Agreement, and such inventions, trade secret and know-how shall remain the exclusive property of Sponsor (collectively “Sponsor’s Property”).

Quintiles’ Property. Any inventions, processes, know-how, trade secrets, improvements, other intellectual properties and other assets, including but not limited to analytical methods, procedures and techniques, procedure manuals, personnel data, financial information, computer technical expertise and software, which have been developed by Quintiles independent of this Agreement, which relates to Quintiles’ business or operations, and not falling within Section 6.3a below, shall remain the exclusive property of Quintiles (collectively “Quintiles’ Property”). For the avoidance of doubt, Quintiles’ Property shall not include any inventions, trade secrets or know-how that incorporates data, information or know-how derived from Sponsor’s Property of Sponsor Confidential Information.

Project Intellectual Property (IP).

Any inventions and discoveries, including any data and information generated or derived by Quintiles as the result of Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement and/or uses Sponsor Confidential Information (collectively “Project IP”) are the sole and exclusive property of Sponsor and Quintiles hereby assigns to Sponsor any Quintiles rights to Project IP (including any patent and all other intellectual property rights therein). Project IP shall be deemed Sponsor Confidential Information for purposes of Section 5.1 above.

Sponsor and Quintiles agree that any Quintiles’ Property or improvements thereto which are used, improved, modified or developed by Quintiles under the term of this Agreement, and which do not use or include any Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor’s Property, are the sole and exclusive property of Quintiles and shall be deemed Quintiles Confidential Information. To the extent the Quintiles Software (defined as programs for the purposes of data derivations, population identification, production of statistical analysis outputs, is determined to be necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data generated as a result of the Services performed by Quintiles under this Agreement, Quintiles grants to Sponsor a royalty-free, non-exclusive license with the right use by only Sponsor (and not its Affiliates or other third parties) without the right to sell, assign or sublicense such software programs and any improvements thereto in connection with such Sponsor project under the Agreement. For such software, Quintiles will provide to Sponsor the macros. When Quintiles’ Software is no longer necessary to access, retrieve or use the study data as described above, such Quintiles Software shall be returned to Quintiles.

No Implied Rights. Except as expressly provided herein, neither party shall have any right, title or interest to or in any patents, patent applications, know-how (whether patentable or not) or other intellectual property rights of the other party.

**IPR-05: Does the clause state limits on how each party may use the other's IP?**
Sponsor's use of Quintiles' software is clearly restricted (no sale, assignment, or sublicense), and 67DE8F74's "no implied rights" language reinforces that neither party gets rights beyond what's expressly granted. **IPR-06: Does the clause deal with third-party IP infringement claims?**
I'm checking whether there's any language addressing this.

**IPR-07: Background vs foreground IP distinction?**
Sponsor's Property and Quintiles' Property serve as background IP, while Project IP represents foreground IP created during performance -- both are defined and allocated, so this is Met.

**IPR-08: Does the clause grant provider unlimited/broad rights to use customer data for its own benefit?**
Quintiles' improvements explicitly exclude any use of Sponsor Confidential Information or Sponsor's Property, and Project IP (including data) assigns back to Sponsor rather than granting Quintiles broad usage rights -- so this is Met, no such grant exists.

Now I want to revisit IPR-03 and IPR-05 more carefully, particularly around the scope of the software license granted to Quintiles.

explanation_call.reason: The Records and Materials clause is entirely silent on any audit right, its permissible scope, required advance notice, frequency, cooperation obligations, correction process, and cost allocation. Without these defined parameters, Quintiles, Inc. is exposed to ad hoc, unscheduled, and potentially unlimited demands from Sponsor for access to Quintiles' records, systems, and premises, with no procedural safeguards to protect Quintiles' operations or limit disruption. The absence of cost allocation is particularly harmful to Quintiles, as Sponsor could otherwise argue that Quintiles must bear audit costs, and the lack of a correction mechanism denies Quintiles a fair opportunity to address any findings before escalation. These omissions should be addressed within this clause, and the resulting audit obligations should be read in conjunction with the confidentiality provisions referenced elsewhere in the Agreement.

Quintiles agrees to retain all records and data generated in the performance of any Project under this Agreement, and other Project-related materials including without limitation Sponsor's proprietary compound ("Records and Materials"), and further agrees to maintain all Records and Materials in a secure area reasonably protected from fire, theft and destruction. clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Regulatory Compliance; Certification; Inspections.

Quintiles agrees that its Services will be conducted in compliance with all applicable laws, rules and regulations, including but not limited to the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the regulations promulgated pursuant thereto, and with the standard of care customary in the contract research organization industry. Regarding the FDA’s electronic records and signatures regulation, 21 CFR Part 11 (“Part 11”), Quintiles has a compliance plan in place as to its applicable database applications and electronic records systems and it is working diligently to implement its plan. Quintiles, however, is not responsible for the compliance or non-compliance of applications or systems used by third parties (including, but not limited to, investigative sites or third party laboratories), or any Part 11 audits or assessments thereof, unless such applications or systems are owned by Quintiles. Quintiles’ standard operating procedures will be used in performance of the Services, unless otherwise specifically stated in the Work Order. Sponsor represents that it will cooperate with Quintiles in taking any actions that Quintiles and Sponsor reasonably believes are necessary to comply with the regulatory obligations that have been transferred to Quintiles hereunder.

Quintiles certifies that it has not been debarred under the Generic Drug Enforcement Act and that it will not knowingly employ any person or entity that has been so debarred to perform any Services under this Agreement. Sponsor represents and certifies that it will not require Quintiles to perform any assignments or tasks in a manner that would violate any applicable law or regulation.

During the term of this Agreement, Quintiles will permit Sponsor’s representatives (unless such representatives are competitors of Quintiles) to examine or audit the work performed hereunder and the facilities at which the work is conducted upon reasonable advance notice during regular business hours to determine that the Project assignment is being conducted in accordance with the relevant Work Order and that the facilities are adequate. Quintiles shall cooperate with Sponsor and allow Sponsor access to relevant records and data to the extent permitted by law. All information (other than Sponsor Confidential Information) disclosed, revealed to or ascertained by Sponsor in connection with any such audit or examination or in connection with any correspondence between Quintiles and any regulatory authorities (including any FDA Form 483 notices) shall be deemed to constitute Quintiles Confidential Information for purposes of this Agreement. Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for its time and reasonable expenses associated with any such audit by Sponsor, unless such audit finds that Quintiles breached this Agreement or any applicable law or regulation.

If any governmental or regulatory agency conducts, or gives notice to Quintiles of its intent to conduct an inspection or to take any regulatory action with respect to any Project or Services pursuant to this Agreement, Quintiles will promptly notify Sponsor prior to complying with such request. Where reasonably practicable, Sponsor will be given the opportunity to have a representative present during any governmental or regulatory inspection. Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for its time and reasonable expenses (including reasonable attorney fees and the costs of responding to findings) associated with any such inspection, unless such inspection finds that Quintiles breached this Agreement or any applicable law or regulation.

- Sponsor's indemnity: "third-party claims, actions, proceedings, investigations or litigation relating to or arising from or in connection with this Agreement, any Work Order, or the Services" - specific triggers are identified.

- This is unambiguous — Sponsor indemnifies Quintiles Indemnified Parties, and Quintiles indemnifies Sponsor. Met.

Looking at the scope comparison, the two indemnities aren't mutual — Sponsor's obligation is broad, covering third-party claims arising from the Agreement/Services except where caused solely by Quintiles' own negligence or misconduct, while Quintiles' obligation is narrower, limited to its own negligence or intentional misconduct. From Quintiles' perspective as the beneficiary of the broader Sponsor indemnity, this asymmetry is favorable since Sponsor bears more risk than Quintiles does under its own narrower indemnity.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Termination.

Sponsor may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order without cause at any time during the term of the Agreement on thirty (30) day’s prior written notice to Quintiles.

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days’ written notice specifying the nature of the breach, if such breach has not been substantially cured within the thirty (30) day period. During the 30-day cure period for termination due to breach, each party will continue to perform its obligations under the Agreement. If the cure period has expired without a substantial cure of the breach, then the parties shall promptly meet to prepare a close-out schedule, and Quintiles shall cease performing all work not necessary for the orderly close-out of the Services or required by laws or regulations.

Either party may terminate this Agreement or any Work Orders immediately upon provision of written notice if the other party becomes insolvent or files for bankruptcy. Any written termination notice shall identify the specific Work Order or Work Orders that are being terminated.

If this Agreement or any Work Order is terminated for reasons other than material breach by Quintiles, Sponsor shall pay Quintiles for all Services properly performed in accordance with any applicable Work Order and reimburse Quintiles for all reasonable costs and expenses incurred in performing such Services, including all non-cancelable costs incurred prior to the termination date. If payments are unit or milestone based, and the Agreement or a Work Order is terminated after costs have been incurred toward achieving portions of one or more incomplete units or milestones, Sponsor will pay Quintiles’ standard fees for actual work performed toward those incomplete units or milestones up to the date of termination (not to exceed the actual amount due for completion of such milestone or unit), in addition to paying for completed units or milestones.

Upon receipt of a termination notice, Quintiles shall promptly cease performing any work not necessary for the orderly close out of the affected Project(s), or for the fulfillment of any regulatory requirements, and will submit an itemized accounting of the Services completed, expenses incurred pursuant to the performance of the Services, any non-cancelable expenses incurred relating to the unfinished Work Order, and payments received in order to determine a balance to be paid by either party to the other. Such balance will be paid within thirty (30) days of receipt of such itemized accounting.

explanation_call.reason: The catch-all limb of the "control" definition — "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" — is substantively vague and contains a typographical error ("polices" for "policies"), both of which expose Quintiles, Inc. to material risk. Because "influence" is a markedly lower threshold than actual legal or contractual control, Sponsor could argue that entities Quintiles merely influences (e.g., minority investees, joint ventures, or strategic partners) qualify as Quintiles affiliates, thereby binding those entities to the Agreement's obligations and extending Quintiles' performance liability across a wider corporate network than intended. Replacing the undefined, subjective standard with the market-standard formulation — "the power to direct the management and policies of an entity, whether through ownership, by contract, or otherwise" — provides an objective, enforceable threshold that protects Quintiles, Inc. from inadvertent over-inclusion of entities outside its actual control.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Relationship with Affiliates; Subcontracts.

Sponsor agrees that Quintiles may use the Services of its corporate affiliates to fulfill Quintiles’ obligations under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any affiliate so used shall be subject to all of the terms and conditions applicable to Quintiles under this Agreement or any Work Order, and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Quintiles under this Agreement and any Work Order. Quintiles agrees that Sponsor’s affiliates may use the services of Quintiles (and its affiliates) under this Agreement. In such event, such Sponsor’s affiliates shall be bound by all the terms and conditions of this Agreement and any Work Order and entitled to all rights and protections afforded Sponsor under this Agreement and any Work Order. Any such affiliate of Sponsor or Quintiles may execute a Work Order directly. The term “affiliate” shall mean all entities controlling, controlled by or under common control with Sponsor or Quintiles, as the case may be. The term “control” shall mean the ability to vote fifty percent (50%) or more of the voting securities of any entity or otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity.

The issue identified is that the definition of "control" contains the phrase "otherwise having the ability to influence and direct the polices and direction of an entity" - which is both vague (undefined standard) and contains a typo ("polices" should be "policies"). The phrase "influence and direct" is a broad, undefined catch-all that could sweep in entities that Quintiles has only minor relationships with, potentially exposing Quintiles to unexpected obligations or restricting its operational flexibility.

For Quintiles, the risk is that the vague catch-all in the "control" definition could be interpreted broadly to include entities that Quintiles merely influences (e.g., joint ventures, minority investments, or strategic partners), subjecting them to all terms and conditions of the Agreement without Quintiles having bargained for this. It could also allow Sponsor to claim that certain entities are "affiliates" of Quintiles based on mere influence, thereby expanding Quintiles' obligations.
I should narrow this to an objective standard, replacing the vague phrase with market-standard language like "otherwise having the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of such entity, whether through ownership of voting securities, by contract, or otherwise," while also fixing the "polices" typo and preserving the rest of the original definition intact.

This is a unilateral discretion granted to Sponsor with no standard or timeframe for approval/denial, meaning Sponsor could withhold or delay approval arbitrarily, operationally paralyzing Quintiles.

2. **Obligation without corresponding benefit/right**: Quintiles must provide "sufficient information to enable proper evaluation" but there's no obligation on Sponsor to respond within a defined timeframe, nor any standard limiting Sponsor's right to withhold approval (e.g., not unreasonably withheld).
There's also some ambiguity in requiring subcontractor agreements to contain provisions "substantially similar to" certain sections, since courts could interpret that loosely, but the approval issue is the bigger concern. The fix should add "not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed" language plus a response deadline or deemed-approval mechanism, and I want to draft this as a surgical, targeted change rather than rewriting the whole clause.

I'll avoid inventing a specific day count and just rely on the "not unreasonably withheld" qualifier. The core problem is that Sponsor holds unchecked, standardless veto power over subcontracting with no response deadline, exposing Quintiles to operational disruption and delay even though Quintiles bears all the subcontracting liability under condition (ii) — making the clause commercially lopsided.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text:
Cooperation; Delays; Disclosure of Hazards.

Sponsor shall forward to Quintiles in a timely manner all documents, materials and information in Sponsor’s possession or control necessary for Quintiles to conduct the Services. Quintiles will use commercially reasonable efforts to complete the agreed upon Services within the timelines set forth in an executed Work Order or Change Order. Quintiles shall not be liable to Sponsor nor be deemed to have breached this Agreement for errors, delays or other consequences arising from Sponsor’s failure to timely provide documents, materials or information or to otherwise cooperate with Quintiles in order for Quintiles to timely and properly perform its obligations under the relevant Work Order or Change Order.

Quintiles and Sponsor agree to notify the other in writing immediately if any delays or limits are encountered in their performance of any Work Order, and shall use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution to such delays or limits.

Sponsor shall provide Quintiles with all information available to it regarding known or potential hazards associated with the use of any substances supplied to Quintiles by Sponsor, and Sponsor shall comply with all current legislation and regulations concerning the shipment of substances by the land, sea or air. Quintiles agrees to comply with all laws, rules and regulations, including written instructions provided by Sponsor, relating to the storage and handling of any such substances received from Sponsor.

Let me analyze this clause carefully from the perspective of Quintiles, Inc. as the represented party.

Let me review each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations**
Looking at the clause:
- [3B52A5DD]: Sponsor must forward documents "in a timely manner" (vague). Quintiles uses "commercially reasonable efforts" to complete services. Quintiles is explicitly protected from liability for Sponsor's failure to cooperate. This is actually somewhat favorable to Quintiles.
- [16AD52BD]: Both parties must notify each other of delays - mutual obligation.
- [80812509]: Sponsor must provide hazard information AND comply with legislation. Quintiles must comply with laws and Sponsor's written instructions regarding storage/handling. 
The requirement that Quintiles follow Sponsor's written instructions without limitation feels somewhat one-sided, though the clause overall gives Quintiles protection from Sponsor-caused delays and places hazard disclosure duties on Sponsor. Weighing these together, I'd call this criterion "Partly met."

For GEN-02, there are several vague time standards here - "timely manner," "immediately," and "timely provide" all lack specific day counts, so this one is Not met.

GEN-03 doesn't apply since the clause covers cooperation, delays, and hazard disclosure rather than any financial amounts or payment terms - Not applicable.

Moving to GEN-04, most terms like "commercially reasonable efforts," "good faith efforts," and "written instructions" have plain commercial meaning, so despite some vagueness around timing, I'll mark this Met.

For GEN-05, while failure to comply with Sponsor's instructions could theoretically create liability exposure for Quintiles, there's no explicit indemnity, warranty, or liability cap language in this specific clause creating unlimited exposure.

I do notice the clause at [3B52A5DD] protects Quintiles from liability for delays caused by Sponsor's failure to provide documents timely, but there's no mirror protection for Quintiles if it fails to follow Sponsor's written instructions.

This creates an asymmetric exposure, but since it's still a compliance obligation rather than an explicit financial or indemnity provision, I'll mark GEN-05 as Not applicable. Moving on, GEN-06 and GEN-07 both look satisfied with no placeholders or contradictions, so I'm now checking GEN-08 for unpaired rights and obligations, starting with Sponsor's right to issue instructions without Quintiles having a corresponding right to object.

For GEN-09, I'm flagging several vague terms like "timely manner" and "immediately," along with the lack of a stated remedy if good-faith negotiations fail, and the unlimited scope of "written instructions provided by Sponsor" which lacks clear boundaries despite the storage/handling qualifier — so I'll mark this as Partly met.

Checking GEN-10, the triggers for notification obligations and compliance duties seem clear enough across the clauses, so that's Met. Now finalizing: GEN-01 Partly met due to one-sided compliance obligations, GEN-02 Not met given multiple vague timing standards, GEN-03 Not applicable since there's no financial component, and GEN-04 Partly met because "timely manner" and "good faith efforts" remain undefined.

explanation_thinking_by_para.80812509:
Let me analyze the issue carefully.

The problem is that Quintiles' obligation to comply with "written instructions provided by Sponsor" effectively elevates Sponsor's unilateral instructions to the same level as legal requirements (laws, rules and regulations). This is one-sided because:

1. Sponsor can issue written instructions at any time without limitation, and Quintiles must comply with them as if they were law.
2. Sponsor's written instructions are not subject to any materiality, reasonableness, or prior notice standard.
3. There's no corresponding obligation on Sponsor to ensure its written instructions are reasonable, lawful, or timely provided.
4. Quintiles bears full compliance risk for Sponsor-issued instructions without any protection if those instructions are themselves unlawful or impossible to follow.
5. There's also an asymmetry between the parties' obligations: Sponsor need only comply with current legislation and regulations on shipment, while Quintiles must comply with laws plus Sponsor's written instructions.

The minimal fix is to qualify the phrase as "reasonable written instructions provided by Sponsor in advance," possibly with a carve-out excusing Quintiles from instructions that would violate applicable law or aren't reasonably practicable.

I'll also add a carve-out so Sponsor's instructions can't conflict with applicable law, keeping the edit minimal and surgical: requiring compliance with "reasonable written instructions provided by Sponsor that do not conflict with applicable law" relating to storage and handling of substances received from Sponsor.

suggestions.reason: The obligation to "use good faith efforts to negotiate an acceptable resolution" imposes no objective or measurable standard on either party, exposing Quintiles, Inc. to a dispute in which a court would need extrinsic evidence to determine whether Quintiles, Inc. discharged its obligation or whether the counterparty's refusal to agree was itself a breach. The clause provides a list with a catch-all phrase, so this criterion is MET.

Looking closer, items like "labor troubles" and "inability to procure materials or services" could arguably fall within a party's control, and the clause doesn't carve those out.

**FOR-06**: Now checking whether the clause addresses what happens to payment during the event, given that payment obligations are explicitly carved out from the excuse.

**FOR-06**: Payment is explicitly carved out from the excuse - MET.

**FOR-08**: No mention of continuity or recovery obligations during the event - NOT MET.

Let me analyze this clause carefully against each criterion from Quintiles, Inc.'s perspective as the reviewed party.

The clause is about Foreign Currency Exchange in a Master Services Agreement. Quintiles is providing services to a Sponsor.

Let me work through each criterion:

**GEN-01: One-sided obligations**
The clause requires Sponsor to reimburse Quintiles for pass-through costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda rate. This seems relatively balanced - Quintiles incurs costs, Sponsor reimburses. However, there's a provision that for Work Orders involving Services in countries with different currencies where fees exceed $500,000, a currency exchange provision "shall be included" in the Work Order - but no mechanism is specified for what happens if one isn't included, or if the parties can't agree. From Quintiles' perspective, this is somewhat one-sided in that it doesn't protect Quintiles if no agreement is reached on the currency exchange provision.
The obligation to include a currency exchange provision for larger fee arrangements leaves open who's responsible for drafting it and what happens if it's omitted or disputed - a gap that could leave Quintiles exposed to currency risk without a clear fallback mechanism.

**GEN-02: Vague time standards**

The timing reference for the Oanda rate is definite enough, but I don't see a specified timeframe for when Sponsor must actually reimburse these pass-through costs - that gap might be covered elsewhere in the MSA, but it's worth flagging here.

**GEN-03/04: Financial amounts and undefined terms**

The dollar threshold and rate mechanism seem clear and determinable, but "pass-through costs" itself isn't defined within this clause.

**GEN-05 through GEN-08**

This clause doesn't impose unlimited liability - if anything it obligates Sponsor to reimburse Quintiles. I don't spot any unfilled placeholders or contradictions, but there's a real gap around who must trigger the currency exchange provision when exposure exceeds $500,000 and what recourse exists if that party fails to include it.

**GEN-09 and GEN-10**

The "shall be included" language is ambiguous since it doesn't assign responsibility, specify required terms, or address what happens absent agreement - two reasonable readers could diverge here. The triggering conditions themselves (non-Contracted Currency services exceeding $500,000, and the Oanda rate reimbursement for pass-through costs) are clearly defined and appear satisfied, so I'm moving into finalizing the GEN assessments, starting with GEN-01 on balance of reimbursement obligations.

The ambiguity over who's responsible for including the currency exchange provision leaves GEN-09 unclear, though GEN-10's triggers are clearly identified. Revisiting GEN-01, the reimbursement benefits Quintiles but the unclear obligation for the >$500K provision could disadvantage them if Sponsor won't agree, so I'll keep that as Partly met. For GEN-02, the reimbursement timing isn't stated here and may be governed elsewhere, while GEN-05 remains Not applicable since no liability exposure arises for Quintiles.

suggestions.reason: The clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material financial and enforcement risk on three fronts. First, the mandate that "a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order" is entirely undefined — it specifies no minimum content, assigns no drafting obligation to either party, and provides no fallback if Sponsor refuses to agree, leaving Quintiles without enforceable currency protection on high-value international Work Orders. suggestions.original_text: Foreign Currency Exchange. The currency to be used for invoice and payment shall be the currency stated in the Budget or Table attached to the Work Order (the “Contracted Currency”). If Quintiles incurs pass-through costs in a currency other than the Contracted Currency, then Sponsor shall reimburse Quintiles for Quintiles’ actual costs in the Contracted Currency based on the Oanda foreign currency exchange rate (Oanda.com) for the applicable currencies on the last business Friday of the month. For Work Orders that involve the performance of Services by Quintiles or its affiliates in any countries that use currencies other than the Contracted Currency, and the fees for such Services will exceed $500,000, then a currency exchange provision shall be included in the Work Order.

explanation_call.reason: The clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to enforcement disputes on two fronts: first, "at the beginning of each calendar year" does not identify a specific effective date or require advance notice, leaving the counterparty room to contest when any increase actually takes effect and potentially withholding payment of adjusted fees; second, the inflation formula's use of "or" between the 4% floor and the Economist index is ambiguous as to which measure governs, allowing the counterparty to insist on whichever figure produces the lower increase and thereby eroding Quintiles' ability to recover its full rising business costs. Additionally, "the equivalent inflation index of the country where services are performed" is undefined, creating a further basis for a counterparty to dispute the applicable measure entirely and block or delay Quintiles' fee adjustment. These combined ambiguities materially undermine Quintiles' ability to exercise and enforce a right that is fundamental to the commercial viability of multi-year engagements.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Inflation Adjustments. Where services in a Work Order are provided by Quintiles over multiple calendar years, Quintiles may increase its fees effective January 1 of each applicable calendar year, upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Customer, to reflect increases in Quintiles' business costs on a prospective basis only. Quintiles' overall costs may be increased for the next twelve (12) month period using the higher of four percent (4%) or the average percentage change in the wages/earnings survey as published in the Economist (or as reported at www.economist.com), or, for services performed outside the United States, the higher of four percent (4%) or the equivalent nationally recognized official inflation index published by the government or central bank of the country where services are performed, in each case over the preceding twelve (12) month period.

explanation_call.reason: As currently drafted, the assignment clause exposes Quintiles, Inc. to material operational and financial risk on several fronts: consent to any assignment is unqualified, meaning Sponsor could unreasonably withhold approval of a Quintiles corporate reorganization, affiliate transfer, or M&A transaction without recourse or time limit. The clause is also silent on the assigning party's continuing liability, leaving Quintiles potentially unable to pursue the original Sponsor obligor if Sponsor transfers its payment or other obligations to a less creditworthy entity. Critically, there is no change-of-control mechanism, so if Sponsor is acquired by a competitor of Quintiles, Quintiles has no contractual right to terminate, nor is Sponsor required to notify Quintiles of such an event. These gaps, taken together, create significant enforceability and counterparty-credit risk for Quintiles across the life of the Agreement.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Binding Agreement and Assignment. This Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of Sponsor and Quintiles and their respective successors and permitted assigns. Except as stated above in Section 17.1, neither party may assign any of its rights or obligations under this Agreement without the express, written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either party may assign this Agreement without consent to an Affiliate or in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, upon prior written notice to the non-assigning party, and in each such case the assigning party shall remain liable for all of its obligations under this Agreement unless expressly released in writing by the other party. Either party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice if the other party undergoes a change of control with a direct competitor of the terminating party.

explanation_call.reason: The clause as drafted exposes Quintiles, Inc. to significant operational and financial risk by deferring all termination mechanics to the Master Agreement without stating any grounds, notice requirements, written form requirements, cure periods, or consequences of termination within the Work Order itself. If the Master Agreement is silent or ambiguous on any of these elements, Quintiles, Inc. has no express contractual basis to terminate for material breach with a defined cure period, no right to payment for completed work upon early termination, and no clarity on when termination actually takes effect. The absence of a termination-for-convenience notice period further leaves Quintiles, Inc. exposed to abrupt termination without adequate protection for costs already incurred. The survival provision is only partially addressed and should be read alongside the Master Agreement's survival clause to confirm that payment obligations and confidentiality obligations survive Work Order termination.
explanation_call.suggested_fix: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is earlier terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement or this Section. Either party may terminate this Work Order for material breach upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice if such breach remains uncured at the expiration of that period, or for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. Termination shall take effect upon expiration of the applicable notice period. Upon termination, Quintiles, Inc. shall be entitled to payment for all services performed and reasonable non-cancellable costs incurred through the effective date of termination. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

clause_units.clause_unit_entire_text: Term. The term of this Work Order shall commence on the date of execution and shall continue until the services described in Attachment 1 are completed, unless this Work Order is terminated in accordance with the Master Agreement. If the Master Agreement is terminated or expires, but this Work Order is not terminated or completed, then the terms of the Master Agreement shall continue to apply to this Work Order until the Work Order is either terminated or completed.

explanation_thinking_by_para.4F1F6DC9:
Let me analyze the issues identified:

1. The clause doesn't specify who may sign an amendment for each party (authorized representatives/signatories)
2. The clause only covers "this Work Order" but not the broader Agreement, including schedules and other orders

For Quintiles, Inc., the risks are:
1. Without specifying authorized signatories, a junior employee or unauthorized person could purportedly execute an amendment, binding Quintiles, Inc. to terms it didn't intend to approve at the appropriate level
2. The scope limitation to "this Work Order" means the Master Services Agreement itself, other schedules, and other orders could be modified informally without written amendment, leaving Quintiles, Inc. 

I want the fix to be minimal and surgical, keeping within roughly ±20% of the original word count while broadening scope to the Agreement (including schedules, exhibits, and Work Orders) and adding a requirement that amendments be signed by authorized representatives of each party.

suggestions.reason: As currently drafted, the amendment clause is limited in scope to "this Work Order," leaving the Master Services Agreement itself and any other Schedules or attachments potentially modifiable without a written, signed amendment — a gap that exposes Quintiles, Inc. to arguments that informal communications or course-of-dealing altered its broader contractual rights. Additionally, the clause does not require execution by an authorized representative of each party, meaning a counterparty could contend that a signature by an employee without actual authority constitutes a binding amendment, undermining Quintiles, Inc.'s internal approval and governance controls. Both deficiencies are commercially material: the first narrows the written-amendment protection to a single Work Order rather than the full contractual framework, and the second removes a threshold safeguard against unauthorized modifications.

Without a binding cost adjustment mechanism, Quintiles, Inc. is exposed to material financial erosion over multi-year engagements where labour, materials, and operating expenses increase but contractual rates remain fixed. The absence of any defined index, adjustment formula, timing, or notice mechanism means no court could enforce this provision as written, and any attempt by Quintiles, Inc. to unilaterally adjust fees would be contractually unsupported and subject to dispute.
suggestions.original_text: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. [Insert cost adjustment provision and inflation provision, if appropriate.]
suggestions.suggested_fix: Inflation and Cost Adjustment. Quintiles, Inc. may adjust the fees for the Services once per calendar year upon not less than sixty (60) days' prior written notice to the other party. Any such adjustment shall not exceed the annual percentage change in the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) as published by the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics for the twelve (12)-month period most recently completed prior to the date of such notice. Adjusted fees shall take effect at the start of the first full calendar month following expiry of the notice period.
